rows.rationale: Three-way match is complete for this GOODS PO (clause 1): PO, receipt GR-7701 and invoice all show 200 EACH at $4.20, so there is no price (clause 3) or quantity (clause 4) variance. Recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate is $63.00, exactly the supplier's figure (clause 5). No non-PO lines, no currency difference, no prior invoices or open credit memos. Net payable $903.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The only discrepancy was unit of measure: the supplier billed 480 EACH @ $2.00 against a PO of 40 CASE @ $24.00 with pack size 12 (vendor.json). Normalised per clause 2 the line reconciles exactly ($960.00, 40 CASE, $24.00/CASE) — a routine conversion, not a defect (clause 11.1). Receipt GR-7702 confirms 40 CASE received (clause 1, 3-way match), price variance is nil (clause 3), and tax recomputes to $72.00 at 7.5% exactly (clause 5). Net payable $1,032.00, no credit memos, AP_CLERK approval per clause 10.

The $1.10/EACH price increase (62.00 -> 63.10, 1.77%) sits inside the clause 3 band, which is the lower of 2% ($1.24) and $50.00, so it is not a defect and the invoiced price is payable. Goods receipt GR-7703 confirms 100 EACH ordered, received and invoiced (clause 4), and tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate is exactly $473.25 (clause 5). No credit memos outstanding; net payable $6,783.25 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $154.00/EACH vs PO $145.00/EACH (+6.21%, $9.00) against an allowance of $2.90 (lower of 2% and $50.00)
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (80 EACH ordered, received, invoiced) and tax recomputes to $924.00 exactly, so the only issue is price. The invoiced unit price exceeds the PO price by 6.21% ($9.00) against a clause 3 allowance of $2.90. The supplier's price notice is a unilateral assertion from its own billing team, not from or countersigned by an authorised buyer (Dele Fashanu / Priya Raman), so it fails clause 3.1 and does not cure the variance. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; hold at $0.00 pending buyer action.

The 6.0% unit-price increase ($88.00 -> $93.28) exceeds the clause 3 band (lower of 2% / $50.00 = $1.76), but is cured under clause 3.1: buyer Dele Fashanu, a listed authorised buyer, approved in writing 'up to 6% on PO-4405, conduit line only'. Receipt GR-7705 confirms 60 EACH received against 60 ordered/invoiced (clause 4), and recomputed tax at 7.5% matches the supplier's $419.76 exactly (clause 5). No defects, no credit memos; $6,016.56 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 100 EACH invoiced, only 60 EACH received (GR-7706, balance of 40 on backorder)
rows.rationale: Goods PO with a valid receipt showing only 60 of 100 EACH delivered (40 on backorder). Under clause 4 the quantity dispute resolves in favour of the receipt: pay 60 x $9.50 = $570.00 net. Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3), and tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% on the corrected net is $42.75, giving $612.75 gross; the supplier's $71.25 tax is simply the consequence of the over-invoiced quantity, not a separate defect. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; $612.75 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Suspected duplicate: same vendor (after name normalisation), same PO-4407, identical gross $3,225.00, 19 days apart, no distinguishing service period
rows.rationale: All five clause 8 duplicate conditions hold against prior PAID invoice NW-9912 (Nordwind Supply Co., PO-4407, $3,225.00, 2026-02-27): normalised vendor name matches, same PO, gross identical within $0.01, dates 19 days apart, and both invoices carry no service period, so clause 8.1 recurring-charge relief does not apply. Price, quantity (25 EACH ordered/received/invoiced) and tax (7.5% = $225.00 exactly) are otherwise clean, so the duplicate is the only defect and no clause 11 escalation is triggered. Payable $0.00 per clause 12; threshold at $0.00 is AP_CLERK.

March retainer matches the blanket SERVICES PO exactly on price and quantity, and tax recomputes to $360.00 at the vendor's 7.5% rate (clauses 3, 5). The identical prior invoice INV-3221 covers 2026-02-01/2026-02-28, a distinct non-overlapping service period, so it is a legitimate recurring charge and not a duplicate (clause 8.1). No goods receipt is expected on a SERVICES PO (clause 1); no credit memos outstanding. Net payable $5,160.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Goods line matches PO and receipt exactly (150 EACH @ $18.00), so no price or quantity variance (clauses 3, 4). The $380.00 expedited freight line is a permitted non-PO charge: contract clause 6.2 expressly allows pass-through of expedited carrier charges up to $500.00, and the receipt note confirms production requested overnight delivery (policy clause 6). Recomputed tax at 7.5% on $3,080.00 is $231.00, matching the invoice exactly (clause 5). No credit memos or prior invoices; net payable $3,311.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Tax overcharge: supplier billed $744.00 tax (12%) versus $465.00 at the vendor's 7.5% rate — $279.00 discrepancy (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Price, quantity and receipt all match exactly (clauses 3, 4, 1). The only defect is tax: at the vendor's 7.5% rate the correct tax on the $6,200.00 net is $465.00, not the $744.00 billed, so the supplier overcharged $279.00 — short-pay the corrected gross of $6,665.00 per clause 5. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; $6,665.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Contract clause 4.2 fixes EUR 1.00 = USD 1.10 for Q1 2026, so the PO price of EUR 210.00 converts to USD 231.00 exactly matching the invoiced unit price — currency conversion under a contract rate is normalisation, not a defect (policy clause 7). Receipt GR-7711 confirms 40 EACH ordered, received and invoiced (clause 4), and recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% is USD 693.00, identical to the supplier's figure (clause 5). No credit memos; net payable USD 9,933.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Over-delivery beyond 5%: 118 EACH received/invoiced against 100 EACH ordered (18% over, tolerance 5 EACH)
rows.rationale: Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3, no variance) and both sides are already in EACH, so no UOM issue. The receipt confirms 118 EACH delivered against a PO for 100 EACH — an 18% over-delivery, far beyond the 5% tolerance in clause 4, so it is a defect requiring receiving/buyer action. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; payable is 0.00 per clause 12 and the approver band for $0.00 is AP_CLERK (clause 10).

PO-4413 is a SERVICES PO, so the absent goods receipt is expected and not a defect (clause 1). Invoiced price matches the PO exactly (clause 3), tax recomputes to $562.50 at the vendor's 7.5% rate (clause 5), and vendor.json holds no prior invoices or open credit memos, so no duplicate or netting applies (clauses 8, 9). Net payable $8,062.50 sits in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 1,050 CASE received against 1,200 CASE invoiced (clause 4)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed $3,240.00 (9%) instead of 7.5% of the corrected net; recomputed tax $2,362.50, delta $877.50 (clause 5)
rows.rationale: UOM normalises cleanly: 30,000 EACH at $1.20 = 1,200 CASE at $30.00/CASE against the PO's $30.00/CASE, so no price variance (clauses 2, 3). Two defects remain: the receipt shows only 1,050 of 1,200 cases delivered, so the line short-pays to $31,500.00 on received quantity (clause 4), and the supplier's tax was billed at 9% rather than the vendor's 7.5%, giving corrected tax of $2,362.50 and gross $33,862.50 (clause 5). Netting open credit memo CM-2026-014 of $1,500.00 gives $32,362.50 (clause 9); two defects plus a payable above $25,000.00 both force escalation to the Controller (clauses 10, 11).

defects: Quantity shortfall: line 4 gland plates invoiced 25 EACH but only 20 received (clause 4, under-delivery)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed 609.84 (9% on uncorrected net) vs 463.20 recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate on the corrected net, delta 146.64 (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Line 2 reconciles exactly once 40 CASE is normalised to 480 EACH at $2.05 (clause 2, not a defect), and line 3's $45.80 vs $45.00 is inside the $0.90 band (clause 3, not a defect). Two defects remain: gland plates were part-shipped, so line 4 pays on 20 received = $2,400.00 (clause 4), giving corrected net $6,176.00; and the supplier applied a 9% tax rate instead of the vendor's 7.5%, so correct tax is $463.20, an overcharge of $146.64 (clause 5). Two defects on one invoice force ESCALATE_HUMAN under clause 11 with recommended payable $6,639.20, AP_CLERK band per clause 10.

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $4,075.00/EACH vs PO $4,000.00/EACH, a $75.00 variance against an allowed band of $50.00 (lower of 2% and $50.00)
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (2 EACH ordered, received and invoiced) and the supplier's tax of $611.25 equals the recomputed 7.5% figure, so clauses 4 and 5 are clean. The single defect is the unit price: $75.00 over the PO price against a clause 3 band of $50.00 (the lower of 2% = $80.00 and the $50.00 per-line cap). No case evidence contains authorisation from a listed buyer referencing PO-4416, so clause 3.1 does not cure it; with one defect only, clause 11 escalation is not triggered and the invoice holds for buyer action under clause 12.

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $19.60/EACH vs PO $18.00/EACH (variance $1.60 vs allowance $0.36); surcharge approved only by Femi Okonkwo, a warehouse supervisor not listed in vendor.json authorised_buyers
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (500 EACH ordered, received, invoiced) and tax reconciles to the cent, so the only issue is price. The $1.60/EACH copper surcharge is 8.89% over the PO price, far outside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $0.36 or $50.00). The only approval referencing PO-4417 comes from Femi Okonkwo, who is not in vendor.json authorised_buyers, so clause 3.1 is not satisfied; Dele Fashanu's authorisation is limited to PO-4405 and expressly excludes other POs. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation: hold for buyer action per clause 12.

defects: Unauthorised surcharge: non-PO delivery and handling line of $640.00 exceeds the $500.00 pass-through limit (clause 6)
rows.rationale: I accept the check's arithmetic and its tax reading: Line 1 is fully supported at $2,460.00 (clauses 3-4, price variance $0.00), and the $232.50 vs $184.50 tax gap is only a consequence of the disputed line, not a second defect. I do not accept the re-labelling. Clause 6 is explicit that a non-PO line failing either condition — here $640.00 against the $500.00 cap, with contract clause 6.3 preserving that limit — is an unauthorised-surcharge defect routed to HOLD_PRICE_VARIANCE, not SHORT_PAY; clause 12 fixes the payable for that disposition at $0.00. The label names the required remedy (buyer action on the surcharge), not the existence of a unit-price variance. If the buyer authorises or the carrier cost is documented and re-cut within the limit, the supported amount to release is $2,460.00 net plus $184.50 tax = $2,644.50.

defects: Tax undercharged: supplier billed $65.00 vs $97.50 recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate (clause 5) — $32.50 tax-compliance exposure
rows.rationale: Price and quantity match exactly (400 EACH at $3.25, fully received per GR-7719), so clauses 3 and 4 are clean. The sole defect is tax: the vendor's 7.5% rate on the $1,300.00 net gives $97.50, not the $65.00 billed. Clause 5 requires paying the recomputed higher total of $1,397.50 while flagging the undercharge; a single defect does not trigger clause 11, and $1,397.50 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Correction accepted on both points: clause 5 requires tax to be recomputed independently rather than taking the supplier's figure, so the payable is the recomputed gross of $1,793.74 (net $1,668.60 + 7.5% = $125.14), not the invoiced $1,793.75. The $0.01 overcharge is inside the $0.02 rounding allowance, so it is not a defect and the disposition stays APPROVE_FOR_PAYMENT. Receipt confirms 206 EACH against 200 ordered — a 3% over-delivery inside the 5% band, payable on the received quantity and not a defect (clause 4); unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3). No credit memos; $1,793.74 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clauses 9–10).

Three-way match is exact: 12 EACH ordered, received and invoiced at the PO price of $118.00/EACH (clauses 1, 3, 4), and recomputed tax at 7.5% equals the supplier's $106.20 (clause 5). The open credit memo CM-2026-021 for $2,000.00 exceeds the $1,522.20 gross, so netting under clause 9 floors the payable at $0.00; netting is not a defect (clause 11.1), and the threshold at $0.00 gives AP_CLERK (clause 10).

The only match trigger is the prior paid invoice HL-3301 (same PO, same $4,300.00, 19 days apart), but it carries a distinct service period (2026-02-01/2026-02-28 vs 2026-02-15/2026-03-14) and the billed name does not normalise to the prior name, so clause 8 is not satisfied and clause 8.1 treats this as a legitimate recurring charge. PO-4422 is a SERVICES PO, so no goods receipt is expected (clause 1); the monthly rate matches the PO exactly and tax of $300.00 equals 7.5% of $4,000.00 (clause 5). Clean invoice, $4,300.00 payable, AP_CLERK per clause 10.

The $242.00/EACH invoiced price exceeds the PO's $220.00 by 10%, outside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $4.40 and $50.00), but is cured under clause 3.1: authorised buyer Priya Raman (vendor.json authorised_buyers) authorised up to $250.00 per enclosure specifically for PO-4423, which covers $242.00. Receipt GR-7723 confirms 15 EACH received against 15 ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and recomputed tax at 7.5% is exactly $272.25 (clause 5). No credit memos; gross $3,902.25 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 60 EACH invoiced, only 52 EACH received (8 kits damaged and refused at the dock) — clause 4 under-delivery
rows.rationale: Receipt GR-7724 shows 52 of 60 kits accepted (8 refused as damaged), so under clause 4 the quantity resolves in favour of the receipt and payment is limited to 52 × $320.00 = $16,640.00 net. Tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate on the corrected net is $1,248.00 (clause 5), giving a corrected gross of $17,888.00; the supplier's $1,440.00 tax is simply the consequence of the over-invoiced quantity, not a separate defect. Unit price matches the PO exactly, so only one defect exists and clause 11 escalation is not triggered; $17,888.00 requires AP_MANAGER approval under clause 10.
